tr_errors.english: If one stage is done by oneself and others are assigned to be done, it is one Sthulatyaya
tr_errors.problem: the source says: if one stage is done, whether oneself or by having another do it, one sthūlātyaya; the English makes it a mixed case

other.note: Translation opens with <meta>The text is from the Vinaya commentary section of the Derge Tengyur, specifically discussing … matchmaking.</meta> — model description shown before the text

tr_errors.english: If one hears that quarrels or disputes will occur even if the ritual is not performed, one should send word to the monks. … After going, one should receive it before the monks.
tr_errors.problem: the rule is that the probationer lays aside (gtang) the observance before a monk when quarrelsome monks arrive and resumes (blang) it after they leave; 'send word' loses the procedure

tr_errors.english: Beat <note>perhaps referring to mats or laundry</note>
tr_errors.problem: speculative note; in this list the beating is most likely of the gaṇḍī

tr_errors.english: If someone becomes attached to the items and acts disrespectfully, they should not be stored away.
tr_errors.problem: sense blurred: the rule is not to fold/put them away disrespectfully

tr_errors.english: One should renounce <note>forbidden behaviors</note> and remove them
tr_errors.problem: guessed note for a sentence continuing from the previous leaf

book_verdict: The Esukhia e-text matches every leaf checked and the translations follow it closely, but the reader text carries model markup: a broken <note> that swallows a paragraph of translation on p. 56 and a <meta> preamble on p. 245, plus one procedural rule garbled on p. 272.
reader_summary: A volume of Vinaya commentary from the Derge Tengyur: rule-by-rule explanations of monastic training rules and of the probation procedure. The Tibetan is the right text for each leaf (a digital e-text aligned to the Derge print). The English is usable for following the argument, but technical rulings need checking against the Tibetan, and leaked note/meta markup interrupts some pages.

reader_summary: A Vinaya word-commentary in the Derge Tengyur that glosses terms from the root text, from martial skills and Brahmin conduct to nuns' garments and false-accusation offences. The Tibetan is the correct text for each leaf. The English reads well and is reliable for the plain glosses, but on offence classifications it sometimes misstates the ruling, and some Sanskrit glosses are the model's guesses.

book_verdict: Right text throughout; the prose commentary pages (340, 480) are translated faithfully, the verse pages less well (a forfeiture category renamed with an invented note, a month misidentified). Esukhia '#' markers and variant braces show in the transcription.
reader_summary: A Derge Tengyur Vinaya volume combining a verse manual of monastic rules (robes, novice precepts) with prose commentary (straining water, the permitted time for meals with an astronomical account of dawn). The Tibetan is the correct text for each leaf, though e-text markers clutter it in places. The English of the commentary is trustworthy; the verse sections are paraphrased into prose and some technical terms are mislabelled.
